newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-WELLINGTON SNAP GAUTENG WINNING RUN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELLINGTON SNAP GAUTENG WINNING RUN.

text.p: Wellington ended the Gauteng Lions' winning streak in the Super 12 rugby series thanks to the pinpoint accuracy of goalkicker Jon Preston, leaving Auckland the only unbeaten team after the Easter break round of matches.
Preston kicked an injury-time penalty at Ellis Park on Saturday to take Wellington to a 37-35 victory over the Lions, formerly Transvaal.
Preston kicked 22 points, six penalties and two conversions and All Black full-back Christian Cullen scored two of Wellington's three tries on his return from injury.
Despite the loss, the Lions remain at the head of the points table with 20, followed by Auckland, Natal, and ACT all with 16 points.
Auckland remained unbeaten with a 49-26 win over Queensland on Monday, but the final score flattered Auckland as Queensland were well in the match until the final 20 minutes.
Auckland stepped up their game in the final quarter and outscored the Australian side six tries to two.
But it was a patchy performance by Auckland, who led 17-6 at halftime, while Queensland's play at times belied their position at the foot of the Super 12 points table.
In other matches, Natal edged New South Wales 28-23 and Orange Free State swamped Otago 49-18 at Invercargill.

Free State kept their game simple and solid and came from behind to lead 21-15 at halftime with three quick tries, then crossed the Otago line four more times in the second half. All seven tries were converted.
Canterbury, playing with just 14 men, pulled off a brave 24-15 win over Waikato after being 10-6 down at halftime.
Canterbury hooker Mark Hammett was sent off for punching opponent Greg Smith 13 minutes into the second half of the floodlit match.

Though Hammett was replaced at hooker, the Crusaders had to lose one player and lock Mark Weedon was pulled off by coach Wayne Smith. All Black Andrew Mehrtens sealed the match with a drop goal in the final minutes.
